newsitem.title: USA: FASB to move ahead on derivatives accounting.
newsitem.headline: FASB to move ahead on derivatives accounting.

text.p: The Financial Accounting Standards Board said Wednesday it has has agreed to move ahead with a final Statement on the accounting for derivatives and hedging.

Although certain issues remain to be resolved, the basic approach in the Statement is to require all derivatives to be recognized in the financial statements and to be measured at fair value, the board said.

Gains and losses resulting from changes in fair values would be accounted for depending on the use of the derivative and whether it is designated and qualifies for hedge accounting. The key criterion for qualification is that the hedging relationship must be highly effective in achieving offsetting changes in fair values or cash flows.

Compared with FASB's 1996 proposal, hedge accounting would be simpler because the effectiveness assessment would be based on the hedging entity's specified risk management objective and strategy, it explained.
The board said it expects to publish the document late in the fourth quarter, and it would take effect January 1, 1999, for calendar-year companies.

"This approach to accounting for derivatives and hedging is a significant improvement over current accounting," said FASB Chairman Edmund L. Jenkins. "It also addresses most of the concerns about our 1996 proposal expressed by constituents in comment letters and the public hearings."
